solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Very much dislike endless swearing (4)

indicatorNotes.endless: a word without its ends loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone who can't stand constant cursing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Swearing" is read as the noun: a single act of swearing, a curse or a solemn vow.
annotation.definitionFit: An oath is a curse or a sworn promise, both kinds of swearing.

entries.clue: Old enclosures originally employed identical means of securing access (4,6)

indicatorNotes.originally: what a word is originally is how it starts, so its first letter

annotation.surface: A history of old fenced enclosures all using the same kind of gate.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about gates and locks, which makes "means of securing access" look literal; the answer is a magic password.
annotation.definitionFit: In the tale of Ali Baba the words open the robbers' cave, so the phrase now means any sure way in.

entries.clue: Work including reference for plant (7)

indicatorNotes.including: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: ref is the usual abbreviation for reference

annotation.surface: A study that cites a source about a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: "Work" and "reference" suggest a book with citations, but work is the labour sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Trefoil is clover or a similar plant, named for its three leaflets.

entries.clue: Son with short hair is totally chilled (10)

blocks.note: s = son, as in family trees
short of hair, i.e. without tresses

annotation.surface: A laid-back boy with a crew cut.
annotation.walkthrough: "Short hair" reads as a haircut, but here "short" means lacking: short of tresses, so tress-less.
annotation.definitionFit: Chilled is slang for relaxed, and the -less suffix makes the answer mean entirely free of tension.

entries.clue: Method of cooking the quince (9)

indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking works the ingredients into a new form

annotation.surface: A recipe step for preparing quinces.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one kitchen instruction, so "Method of cooking" looks like the whole definition; only "Method" is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a way of doing something is both a method and a technique.

entries.clue: Half of Polperro is north of river? That’s not right (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase standing for the noun

indicatorNotes.Half of: take one half of the word, here the back four letters
indicatorNotes.north of: in a down clue, north of means placed above, so first

annotation.surface: A pedant correcting a claim that part of a Cornish village lies north of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: Polperro is a fishing village in Cornwall; only its spelling matters here.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying "that's not right" is pointing out a mistake.

entries.clue: See disruption when travelling appearing quite by chance (13)

indicatorNotes.when travelling: letters on the move end up in a new order

annotation.surface: A traveller's delays that turn up out of the blue.
annotation.walkthrough: "Disruption when travelling" reads as rail delays, and "See" as a plain verb rather than fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Serendipity is a happy accident, so something serendipitous turns up by lucky chance.

entries.clue: Composer and novelist, but not a painter (2,5)

indicatorNotes.but not a: the letter A is taken out

blocks.note: Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose

annotation.surface: Someone who composes and writes novels but can't paint.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says the answer is not a painter, yet "painter" is the definition: the "not a" only removes one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of Renaissance Spain.

entries.clue: Indifferent seamstress’s action reportedly needs repeating (2-2)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, not read, so go by sound
indicatorNotes.needs repeating: something that needs repeating must be said a second time, so the word appears twice

blocks.note: a seamstress sews; say it twice

annotation.surface: A half-hearted dressmaker whose stitching has to be redone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Indifferent" means mediocre here, not uncaring, though the surface reads it as the seamstress's attitude.
annotation.definitionFit: Indifferent in its sense of middling quality, neither good nor bad.

entries.clue: Lamenting in English and Gaelic in translation (7)

indicatorNotes.in translation: a translation renders the same material in a new form, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: A mournful poem rendered into both English and Gaelic.
annotation.walkthrough: The added E sits inside the anagram, so all seven letters are shuffled together.
annotation.definitionFit: An elegy is a lament, and elegiac verse is mournful in tone.

entries.clue: Bury story which correspondents have? (13)

annotation.definitionNote: a cryptic description of the noun: what correspondents share

blocks.note: a relation is a telling, a story

annotation.surface: Journalists hiding a scoop they share.
annotation.walkthrough: Correspondents here are things that correspond to each other, not letter-writers or reporters.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that correspond stand in a mutual relation, an interrelation.

entries.clue: Few reactions are produced by this remarkable talk (4,3)

annotation.definition: Few reactions are produced by this
annotation.surface: A brilliant speech that leaves the audience strangely unmoved.
annotation.walkthrough: The reactions are chemical ones: the rare (noble) gases such as neon and argon barely react with anything.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare gases are chemically inert, so few reactions involve them.

entries.clue: Film within country house, one at Bisley, perhaps? (8,5)

blocks.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

annotation.surface: A film being shot on location at a stately home.
annotation.walkthrough: Bisley, in Surrey, is home to Britain's National Shooting Centre. "Within" looks like a container instruction but simply supplies IN.
annotation.definitionFit: Bisley has many shooting ranges; "perhaps" marks it as one example.

entries.clue: Narrow point’s not let fluid into stream (10)

indicatorNotes.fluid: something fluid has no fixed shape, so the letters flow into a new order
indicatorNotes.into: the anagram goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: beck is a northern English word for a stream

annotation.surface: A narrowing channel that won't allow water into a brook.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fluid" reads as a noun, the water refused entry, but it is an adjective telling NOT LET to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: The narrow neck of a bottle slows the pour, so the word names any point where flow is choked.

entries.clue: Rise skywards bearing light, initially like the sun (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the word's first letter is used

blocks.note: to soar is to rise high

annotation.surface: The dawn sun climbing and bringing light.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes a sunrise, so the definition sits inside its own picture.
annotation.definitionFit: Solar comes from Latin sol, the sun, and describes what belongs to or resembles it.

entries.clue: Bellringer for the Sunday following Easter (9)

blocks.note: the hunchback bellringer of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel
the old church name for Low Sunday, taken from the first words of that day's Latin introit

annotation.surface: A church rota assigning a bellringer for the week after Easter.
annotation.walkthrough: Hugo named his foundling Quasimodo because he was found on Quasimodo Sunday, from the introit "Quasi modo geniti".
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: Hugo's bellringer and the first Sunday after Easter.

entries.clue: Strain with landlord and distant form of communication (3,6)

blocks.note: a strain is a tune, an air
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

annotation.surface: Tension with a landlord conducted by long-distance mail.
annotation.walkthrough: "Strain" suggests stress, but it is the musical sense. An air letter is a lightweight sheet that folds into its own envelope for airmail.
annotation.definitionFit: An air letter carried messages overseas by airmail.

entries.clue: Small mammal tick gets treated always (5,4)

blocks.note: a tick and a mo are both a moment
treated, as in used well or badly
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

annotation.surface: A parasite on a small animal that is forever being dealt with.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tick" suggests the parasite, but it is the British "just a tick", a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: The mouse deer, or chevrotain, is a tiny hoofed mammal.

entries.clue: Eclipse increases thanks to gravitational constant energy (7)

blocks.note: G is the symbol for the gravitational constant

annotation.surface: An astronomy note about an eclipse growing because of gravity.
annotation.walkthrough: "Eclipse" looks like the astronomical noun in a physics surface, but it is a verb meaning outshine.
annotation.definitionFit: From the theatre: an actor who moves upstage forces others to turn away from the audience, stealing the scene, just as one light eclipses another.

entries.clue: Valuable metal obtained after mine is stripped (5)

indicatorNotes.after: the first piece comes after the second
indicatorNotes.stripped: the word loses its outer layer, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Precious ore taken once a mine is worked out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stripped" suggests an exhausted mine, but it strips the word MINE of its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast bar of metal, typically gold or silver.

entries.clue: Relevant language, close to legalese (7)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

annotation.surface: Pertinent wording that sounds almost like legal jargon.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close to" reads as "similar to", but it means the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a germane point is one relevant to the matter in hand.

entries.clue: Show real stamina and support those people failing to complete programme? (4,3,6)

annotation.definition2: support those people failing to complete programme?

blocks.clueFragment: support those people failing to complete programme?
blocks.note: stay = prop up; the course = the students of a course who are flagging

annotation.surface: A pep talk about stamina and helping classmates who are dropping out.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: a stay is a support, so to stay the course is to prop up a whole course's struggling students.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from horse racing, where a horse with stamina lasts the whole distance.

entries.clue: Cover for furniture all the way over width (5)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over puts the first piece on top of the second

blocks.note: thro' = through, as in right through

annotation.surface: A cloth pulled right across a sofa's width.
annotation.walkthrough: THRO is the informal short spelling of through, as in "open Monday thro' Friday".
annotation.definitionFit: A throw is a blanket tossed loosely over a sofa or bed.

entries.clue: On the edge of one’s seat since the beginning of Grease (4)

annotation.definition: On the edge of one’s seat

indicatorNotes.the beginning of: a word's beginning is where it starts, so its first letter

blocks.note: since = ago, as in long since

annotation.surface: A filmgoer gripped from the opening of Grease.
annotation.walkthrough: "Since the beginning" reads as one time phrase, but it splits: since gives AGO, the beginning of Grease gives G.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone agog is eagerly excited, as a gripped audience is.

entries.clue: Moving ice with a lot of dazzling light around? (7)

annotation.definition: Moving ice with a lot of dazzling light around?

indicatorNotes.Moving: the letters move into a new order
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the word, its last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.around: one piece goes round the other

annotation.surface: A glacier glittering in bright sunshine.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a glacier is moving ice, and snow glare surrounds it.
annotation.definitionFit: A glacier is a river of ice creeping downhill, and its surface throws off blinding glare.

entries.clue: Like model operatic role — a recurring duo in La Belle Hélène? (2,5)

blocks.clueFragment: a recurring duo in La Belle Hélène
blocks.note: the pair LE appears in both Belle and Hélène

annotation.surface: A model singing an opera part in Offenbach's La Belle Hélène.
annotation.walkthrough: La Belle Hélène is an Offenbach operetta, but it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A model built to scale keeps the proportions of the original.

entries.clue: Environmentalists protect ancient grassy area (10)

blocks.note: ward is an old word for protect, surviving in ward off

annotation.surface: Campaigners defending an old meadow.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ancient" looks as if it describes the grassland, but it marks WARD as archaic.
annotation.definitionFit: Sward is an old word for turf, so a greensward is a stretch of green grass.

entries.clue: Idiot sometimes seen being followed by chicken? (4)

annotation.definition2: sometimes seen being followed by chicken?

blocks.note: informal, chiefly American, for a stupid person

blocks.clueFragment: sometimes seen being followed by chicken?
blocks.note: a Jamaican spice rub and cooking style, often named before the meat on menus

annotation.surface: A fool spotted with a chicken trailing after him.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: the word often comes before "chicken", as in jerk chicken.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a contemptible fool, and the spicy Jamaican style of cooking meat.
